close_reason:
Replaced both hand-rolled abbreviation tables in utils.rs (23 lines total) with chrono's locale-independent %a (short weekday) and %b (short month) format specifiers. Both emit byte-identical English C-locale strings regardless of host OS locale, so the wire contract on the format output is preserved exactly.

Net change: -17 lines, +0 behavior change. The hand-rolled month-table catch-all defense added in .59 (commit 3cc7eab) becomes unnecessary — there's no match arm anymore. All 8 utils::tests pass unchanged.

cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings clean, fmt clean. Committed as 125dfeb.
description: utils.rs:48-56 (weekday match) and 60-72 (month match) hand-roll match arms that convert chrono::Weekday / chrono month-number to three-letter abbreviations. chrono already provides format specifiers '%a' (abbreviated weekday) and '%b' (abbreviated month) that emit the same strings, well-tested and locale-aware. The hand-rolled match arms total 23 lines and could be: 'parsed.format("%a").to_string()' (one line). Engineering basis: less code, no risk of typo (e.g. 'Tuc' for 'Tue'), leverages chrono's tested implementation. Counter-argument: the hand-rolled match arms keep the strings under the crate's control and avoid any locale surprise — but chrono's '%a' and '%b' are explicitly the English C-locale defaults regardless of system locale, which is what the current code wants. The counter-argument doesn't survive.
title: utils.rs hand-rolled weekday/month abbreviation tables duplicate chrono::format
